sections.name: File setup, polygon, multiPolygon
sections.title: Test setup and sample shapes
sections.what: Brings in the functions under test and defines a sample square and a sample two-part shape.

sections.name: GeoJSON validation
sections.title: Shape validation checks
sections.what: Checks that closed polygons and multi-part shapes are accepted, that malformed nesting, empty shapes, unclosed or short outlines are rejected, that out-of-range or non-numeric coordinates and unsupported types are rejected, and that very large payloads are rejected.
sections.why: Keeps bad shape data from reaching area calculations or storage.
sections.watch_out: The size check is tested with a padding field, so it depends on the size limit value.

sections.name: deterministic geometry area
sections.title: Area calculation check
sections.what: Checks that the same shape always gives the same area, and that the square metre, hectare and acre values are produced for both shape types.
sections.watch_out: The second half of this check was cut off in the packet, so its exact figures could not be confirmed here.

sections.name: synthetic geometry persistence
sections.title: Stored demo shape correction checks
sections.what: Checks that the hero demo's stored shape gives about 1.02 acres after correction, that only the known old seed values are corrected and repeated runs are harmless, that the control demo is corrected to about 1.25 acres, and that a stored user shape is never overwritten. The last check adds a temporary row and removes it at the end.
sections.why: Protects the demo figures and makes sure real user data is left alone.
sections.watch_out: The temporary row is removed only if every earlier check passes, so a failure can leave test data behind.

summary: Tests the geometry service: that land shape data is validated strictly, that areas are calculated consistently, and that the saved demo land shapes are corrected once and never overwrite user shapes.
purpose: Protects the accuracy of land area numbers and the safety of stored shape data.
why: Likely reason: wrong land shapes produce wrong area figures, which matter to land owners, so the tests are thorough.
how: Tests run the validator on good and bad shapes, calculate areas and compare them with expected values, then run the seed correction against the stored database and check the results and the rows.
inputs: Sample shapes, the demo cases, and whatever database the environment selects.
outputs: Pass or fail results. Writes a temporary test row and removes it at the end.
risks: The cleanup of the test row happens only at the end of a test, so if an earlier check fails, the row stays in the shared database.
debug: If a stored shape check fails, look at the stored geometry for the demo case and at the seed correction. If the row count check fails, look for leftover test rows.
